# PEN-4447 — declare the model registry closed and resolve it per agent config

**Files:** `src/server/models.ts`, `src/server/index.ts`, `src/server/models.test.ts`

Paperclip's `PATCH /agents/:id` accepted any string as `adapterConfig.model` and
returned 200. The id is not consumed until the agent's next pod boot, so a wrong
one kills the lane hours later with nothing linking it back to the write. It is
worse than a typo class because the valid ids differ per adapter: `claude-haiku-4-5`
is registered by the in-tree `claude_local` adapter and is **not** in this
adapter's `DIRECT_MODELS` (the cheap floor here is `claude-haiku-4-6`), so the id
chosen on PEN-2514 precisely because it looked like the safest possible write is
the one that would have bricked a `claude_k8s` lane.

Two additions, both additive:

- `modelRegistryIsClosed: true` on the server module — tells Paperclip this
  registry enumerates everything the runtime accepts, so it may refuse an
  unlisted id at the write. Enforcement is opt-in host-side; adapters that
  discover models from a live API must not set it.
- `listK8sModelsForConfig(adapterConfig)` — same lists as `listK8sModels()`, but
  the Direct/Bedrock branch is decided from the **agent's** env rather than this
  process's. Each agent runs in its own Job pod whose env is the inherited server
  env with `adapterConfig.env` layered over it (`job-manifest.ts` layer 4 "wins
  over everything"; `CLAUDE_CODE_*` and `ANTHROPIC_*` are both inherited), so a
  Bedrock lane can exist on a non-Bedrock server and vice versa. Validating
  either against `listK8sModels()` alone would refuse an id that is correct for
  the pod it runs in.

`listK8sModels()` is unchanged, and so is every list. A host that predates the
`ServerAdapterModule` fields simply ignores both.

## Revision after review (PR #2901)

Ally's consolidated review found the first cut's admissible set too narrow — it covered the picker
list, not everything the runtime accepts, so configurations that boot fine today would have been
refused. Two additions:

- `listK8sModelsForConfig` now also returns the CLI aliases (`opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` /
  `opusplan`, with and without `[1m]`). `claude --model opus` is valid configuration and is in no
  registry. They are deliberately NOT added to `models`: that list feeds the picker, which should
  keep showing canonical ids.
- `acceptsK8sModelForConfig` / `isBedrockModelId` accept an id no list can enumerate — a Bedrock
  inference profile under any region prefix (`us.` / `eu.` / `apac.`), a bare `anthropic.*` id, or
  an `arn:aws:bedrock:` ARN. `BEDROCK_MODELS` was being read as the admissible set; it is a
  convenience list. The predicate is gated on the config actually resolving to Bedrock, so a
  Bedrock-shaped id on a direct lane is still refused.

Paperclip separately narrowed enforcement to a model id a write INTRODUCES, so an agent already
carrying an unlisted id is not locked out of unrelated repairs.
